title: Verify Claims, Not Scores: Evidence-Based Verification of Modular Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.01348v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When developers change one component of an agent, such as its controller, a learned model or its verifier, they usually judge the change by an aggregate task score. That score cannot tell whether improvement was attainable, which component lost value, or what the agent's own checks certify. We introduce a claim-specific verification audit for modular agents that plan, act, check and refine. Instead of scoring the agent, the audit scores the evidence: each conclusion is recorded with the evidence behind it, one of four verdicts (supported, unsupported, unresolved or not evaluated) and the boundary within which it holds. Three tools supply that evidence. Oracle policies measure attainable improvement under an explicitly stated action set, so that a low value can be traced to the evaluation rather than to the environment. translated_title: 验证声明而非分数：基于证据的模块化智能体验证
translated_abstract: 当开发者更改智能体的某个组件（例如其控制器、学习模型或验证器）时，他们通常通过聚合任务分数来判断这一更改的效果。然而，该分数无法说明改进是否本可实现、哪个组件损失了价值，或者智能体自身的检查能够证明什么。我们为能够规划、行动、检查和改进的模块化智能体引入了一种针对特定声明的验证审计方法。该审计不是给智能体打分，而是评估其证据：每个结论都与其背后的证据一同被记录，并附上四种判定之一（已支持、未支持、未解决或未评估）以及其成立的边界范围。三种工具提供这些证据。Oracle策略在明确声明的动作集合下衡量可实现的改进，从而可以将低分追溯到评估过程而非环境本身。每次用一个完美对应物替换一个组件来定位损失的价值，并将零结果解读为未解决……
tldr: 该论文提出一种针对模块化智能体的基于证据的验证审计方法，通过记录每个结论的证据、四种判定结果及其成立边界，取代传统聚合任务分数来评估智能体组件变更的有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces an evidence-based verification audit for modular agents that evaluates component changes by recording each conclusion with its supporting evidence, one of four verdicts, and its applicability boundary, instead of relying on aggregate task scores.
